answer: Persistent work ledger. Each identity accrues a public record of verified compute, and rewards scale with cumulative history depth; a fresh node starts near zero and must climb toward its zenith across many paid cycles. To forge that history cheaply, an attacker pays real compute plus a lag penalty at every step, so each clone costs the full repeat price rather than a one-time fee. Marginal cloning thus grows superlinearly, like an ocean of small debts compounding, making mass duplication economically irrational.
